items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: So I went to him, and the old man liked me. And he taught me the rest of the way.

ctx.x: And he began to give me lessons. Then Piron had a deal to go -- the first southern big band to go to New York to play at the Roselond Ballroom. So Lorenzo Tio -- his uncle was a great clarinetist because the whole family, all the men from the great-grandfather on down, were all clarinetists, magnificent clarinetists. And the old man, he didn't want to be bothered with pupils anymore because he couldn't stand them if they couldn't do what he wanted them to do. They'd make him nervous.

But Lorenzo, his nephew, begged him to take me because he said he saw possibilities in me. So the old man said, "Okay. Well, send him on." So I went to him, and the old man liked me. And he taught me the rest of the way.
